title: This Is the Oldest Peace Treaty Ever Discovered - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHistoryThis Is the Oldest Peace Treaty Ever DiscoveredMaybe there are a few things we can still learn from itDNBy David Nield1:30 PM CDT on October 12, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe history of peace treaties goes back to around 1269 BCE, when Pharaoh Ramses II of Egypt and King Hattusilli III of the Hittite Empire put together what’s thought to be the first ever agreement between nations that hostilities should cease: in this case, over disputed Syrian territories. Over the last 120 years, archaeologists have unearthed fragments of this treaty in the ruined Hittite capital—and they just turned up another piece of the original.Discovered in the rocky Büyükkale site in modern-day Türkiye, it contains articles 12 though 20 of the agreement and covers rules around how refugees should be treated, specifically stating that their homes shouldn’t be destroyed. Read more: “Eating for Peace”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
